elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice
elements.evidence: "Customer may terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time upon 90 days' written notice to HDI"

elements.element: Pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on Customer convenience termination
elements.evidence: No refund language; instead "the Company shall pay to HDI a termination payment"

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term
elements.evidence: "unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice" operates only against automatic renewal on each anniversary, not mid-term
"Customer may terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time upon 90 days' written notice to HDI"

elements.element: Early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: "divided by two, but not exceeding 3 months' fees"

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term
elements.evidence: "shall be automatically renewed for an additional one year period on each anniversary of the Effective Date, unless terminated by either Party" — HDI's right bites only at each anniversary/end of term

elements.element: Vendor's end-of-term termination on 90 days' notice
elements.evidence: "unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other"

reasons: All three fallback limbs are satisfied in operative text: an express Customer convenience right at 90 days' notice (within the 60–90 day band), a hard cap on the Termination Payment at 3 months' fees, and HDI's pre-existing termination right that operates only against annual renewal on 90 days' notice.
Preferred level is not met (90 rather than 30 days' notice, no pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and an early-termination fee remains), consistent with the locked fallback target.
Edits are surgical: one short insertion supplying the absent Customer right plus a seven-word cap appended to the existing formula; the term, renewal mechanic and Net Sales formula remain effective.

Minor drafting note (rationale-level only): "3 months' fees" is not a defined term in a Net Sales-based agreement, so tying the cap to the contract's fee/payment provision would remove residual ambiguity; the alias gloss "Customer means the Company" is necessary and adds no substantive term.
